 OmniBot runs directly on your Android device and combines chat, agent tools, local workspaces, and system integrations in one app.
 🎉 Our iOS & macOS version: ViaVera

OmniBot is an on-device AI agent built with native Android Kotlin and Flutter. Instead of stopping at chat, it focuses on the full loop of understand - decide - execute - reflect .

 Core Capabilities 

- Extensible tool ecosystem : Skills, Alpine environment, browser access, MCP, and Android system-level tools.
- System-level actions : Supports scheduled tasks, alarms, calendar creation/query/update, and audio playback control.
- Personal context : Query authorized calendars, contacts, notifications, app usage, location, media, documents, SMS and call history without root, and manage calendar events and contacts.
- Memory system : Short-term and long-term memory with embedding support.
- Productivity tools : Read and write files, browse the workspace, use the browser, and access the terminal.

 
 
 

 
 Quick Start 

 Configure the app

Open the settings page from the left sidebar:

 
 
 
 

Then open the scenario model settings:

 
 
 

Note: Memory embedding requires an embedding model. For the best overall experience, the other scenarios should use multimodal or vision-capable models whenever possible.

 
 
 

The app usually initializes the Alpine environment automatically on startup, and you can also manage that environment from the same settings area.

 Native Gemini connection

Select Gemini in model provider settings, enter an API key, and keep the default base URL Select a model for the built-in Agent. This connection uses the Interactions API for streamed replies, images, thinking levels, and local/MCP tools. External Agents require a Provider using their supported protocol.

Interactions use store=false . Original model steps and signatures are saved in local conversation history for subsequent turns and reopening a conversation. Older history without signatures is supplied as text. Context compaction preserves the active tool cycle. Google Search, Deep Research, and server-side background tasks are not enabled by this connection.

 Use Cases 

 Personal context

Enable individual sources in Settings → App permissions → Personal context . AI queries shared device tools on demand; results may be sent to your configured model and are not automatically added to long-term memory. Calendar and contact read/write permissions are separate. Background location needs its own “Allow all the time” grant. Approximate location and selected-only photo access are supported.

Notification access is separate from receiving Omnibot notifications. Observed notifications are cached locally for up to 7 days and 10,000 records, excluded from system backups, and can be cleared manually. Previously dismissed notifications and system-redacted content cannot be recovered. Revocation stops recording and querying without deleting conversations.

File queries return metadata first; requested contents are imported into the existing file inbox. Files and folders can be selected and access removed through the system-picker entry. SMS and call history are read-only and depend on installer/system eligibility; Omnibot does not request default SMS, phone or assistant roles. These features require neither root, Shizuku nor accessibility and do not access other apps' private databases.

Device MCP and the built-in Agent share tool definitions and execution. context capabilities reports actual access; missing permissions do not open dialogs or terminate ordinary chat. Contact mutations use rawContactId and version from queries and affect only the selected account record. Calendar queries accept an offset ; all-day dates use UTC and an exclusive end date.

 Optional Root and device controls

Direct Root access is off by default. Enable Root access under Settings → App permissions → Advanced Access to request authorization from your device's Root manager. When available, direct Root takes priority over Shizuku; disabling it stops its commands and persistent shells. Shizuku remains independently available.

The agent can query and change supported system toggles, display and sound settings, manage app permissions, run diagnostics, and execute privileged shell commands. Mutations and shell commands require ACP client confirmation. State changes are checked against the device before being reported as successful; unsupported ROM interfaces return an explicit error. See Android privileged actions for the tool contract and compatibility details.

 Skills

You can ask OmniBot to install a skill by simply sending it the repository link. Recommended collection: 

Enable or disable skills from the skill repository:

 
 
 
 

 Scheduled tasks

 
 
 
 

Scheduled tasks execute subagent flows. Alarms are reminder-only. A subagent can be assigned a complete task and behaves like a full agent.

 Workspace

 
 
 

 Remote Codex bridge

To use Codex mode with Codex running on a PC or Mac, start codex-bridge on the computer where the Codex CLI is installed and logged in:

 

Choose the LAN address and token mode in the terminal setup UI, then scan the printed QR code from OpenOmniBot's Codex settings. For advanced options and troubleshooting, see the codex-bridge README.

 

 Development Guide 

 Requirements

- Flutter SDK 3.47.2+ 
- JDK 17+ 
- Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ and pnpm 10.28.0 (for WebUI development)

 Get the code

 

If Flutter reports Could not read script '.../ui/.android/include flutter.groovy' , run:

 

 Develop the WebUI locally

The WebUI in webchat/ is a standalone React + TypeScript + Vite project. During local development, Vite serves the frontend with hot reload and proxies /webchat/api requests to the Android app's local service.

install.title: Build and install
install.html:
Android builds use OMNIBOT_UPDATE_WORKER_URL for the website backend's update checks, anonymous statistics, cloud policy, and official VLM proxy configuration. It defaults to https://omnibot.omnimind.com.cn; upstream proxy credentials stay on the backend. See the integration notes. Debug APK builds use the OpenAI-compatible LLM API configured by LLMTHU_API_BASE, LLMTHU_API_KEY, and LLMTHU_MODEL for normal LLM requests, context compaction, and scene.vlm.operation.primary. For local acceptance testing, Release builds can explicitly enable -POOB_BUNDLE_LLMTHU_PROVIDER=1 to bundle the same LLMTHU_* configuration for use out of the box. Regular Release and CI builds do not bundle this configuration by default.

cd ..

./gradlew :app:installDevelopStandardDebug -Ptarget=lib/main_standard.dart

For acceptance testing on a physical device, use the repository's LLMTHU installation script. It enables the LLMTHU provider by default and reads the API key from LLMTHU_API_KEY in the current shell. If the key is missing, the script fails immediately instead of producing an unusable test APK. Regular Release and CI builds still do not automatically bundle the key.

export LLMTHU_API_KEY='your-api-key'
./scripts/install_release_llmthu_device.sh
